glosses: Alternative spelling of hon (“affectionate abbreviation of honey”).

examples.text: So social media has broken even Elon Musk. I’m forced to ask: U OK hun? [title]

glosses: A woman perceived as basic, brash, working class and fond of alcohol.

examples.text: Answer: you are a hun – but a high-end hun, one who knows her wine, her music, her interiors and her labels, and whose reluctance to do Dry January, or go vegan makes her such great company, this month and every month.

It’s no wonder she’s become a central figure in “hun culture” – an online subculture that idolises a certain strata of famous working-class British women, while also taking the mick out of her leopard print kettle and weakness for a premixed gin-in-a-tin cocktail.

glosses: A woman involved in a multi-level marketing scheme, especially one who pushes it on social media.

examples.text: This corporate love-bombing can serve a hun well, bagging them new downlines and potentially more money (MLMs are renowned for extremely low pay).
Instead of blaming MLM "huns," we should direct our anger at the companies that are knowingly putting so many people in debt and alienating them from their communities.

glosses: Alternative form of hoon (“Indian gold coin”).
A member of a nomadic tribe (the Huns) who invaded Europe in the fourth century from Central Asia.
A vandal, a barbarian, an uncivilized destructive person.

examples.text: Doubtless the first German band to return to England will be composed of the most gentle peace and beer-loving Huns that ever visited our favoured shores.

glosses: A Rangers Football Club supporter; an Orangeman.

glosses: Personne du peuple nomade originaire de l’Eurasie centrale dont la présence en Europe est attestée à partir du IVᵉ siècle.

examples.text: La chanson « Attila le Hun » de Hervé Christiani m’a inspiré la nouvelle éponyme.
Ils étaient toujours plus nombreux, comme si tout Rome s’était rassemblé dans le parc pour voir le Hun enfermé dans la cage.
Bientôt les Huns apparurent sur la rive droite, et, le même jour, on vit l’incendie s’allumer sur tout l’horizon, c’est-à-dire depuis Colonia Agrippina, jusqu’à Aliso.

examples.text: Unter ihrem König Attila eroberten die Hunnen weite Teile Europas.
